newsitem.title: FRANCE: French job creation law seen in place by October.
newsitem.headline: French job creation law seen in place by October.

text.p: Draft legislation to back up the creation of 350,000 jobs for young people in the public sector in France should be in place by around October, government sources said on Tuesday.

The sources confirmed that the estimated cost of state-aided employment creation projects would amount to about 35 billion francs ($5.7 billion) over five years -- with about two billion francs earmarked for this year and 10 billion next year.
Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, who has said his new Socialist government's job creation plan will not need new state spending, met several ministers on Tuesday to put final touches to the bill.

The sources said the three-hour meeting settled almost all the outstanding issues and the bill is due to be sent to cabinet for approval on August 20 before presentation to parliament for adoption in October.

The aim is to filter state funds to job creation projects proposed at local level with the involvement of local authorities and associations, with either indefinite employment contracts or contracts for a minimum of five years, the sources said.

Jospin's team, which took over from the previous centre-right government in early June, has declared employment its top priority and pledged to create 350,000 jobs in the public sector over five years.
It has also pledged to push for the creation of a similar number of jobs, also mainly for young people, in the private sector.

The jobs which would qualify for state assistance under the new legislation on the public sector side would go to people of under 26 years and to people up to age 30 if they have not drawn unemployment benefit since leaving education, the sources said.

Employment Minister Martine Aubry, second-in-command to Jospin and the minister in charge of the legislation, hopes the new law will support the emergence of "new jobs" in mainly social domains, such as help for handicapped people in transport or homework assistance for children, and also in environmental projects.

Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn has said the bulk of the funding for the jobs initiative will be generated by reorganising an already extensive array of job incentive programmes judged to be less efficient.
The sources did not elaborate on the precise plans for generating the 10 billion francs earmarked for 1998.
The plan is to get the legislation into place and create about 50,000 jobs by the end of this year and a further 100,000 next year. ($ = 6.191 Francs)
